name: Rivaroxaban
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 20 mg once daily with the evening meal (15 mg if CrCl ≤50 mL/min)
15 mg twice daily with food for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily with food

usual_adult_dose.indication: Reduce recurrent DVT/PE (after at least 6 months)
DVT prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement

usual_adult_dose.dose: 2.5 mg twice daily with aspirin 75 to 100 mg once daily

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir)
Combined P-gp and moderate CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., erythromycin) with CrCl 15 to <80 mL/min
key_interactions.action: Do not use unless benefit justifies risk.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampin, St. John's wort)

key_interactions.action: Weigh the need; watch for bleeding.

serious: Stroke and thrombotic events after premature discontinuation (boxed warning)

monitoring: Creatinine clearance before starting and periodically (dose and avoidance thresholds)
Signs of bleeding; hemoglobin when indicated

pk.bioavailability: About 66% (20 mg fasting); higher with food
pk.half_life: 5 to 9 hours (age 20 to 45); 11 to 13 hours (age 60 to 76)
pk.half_life_eskd: About 8.6 hours (single 10 mg dose, anuric hemodialysis patients; De Vriese 2015)
pk.metabolism: CYP3A4/5 and CYP2J2; P-gp and BCRP substrate
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 36% unchanged in urine (mainly tubular secretion); 30% as inactive metabolites in urine
pk.dialyzability: No: not dialyzable owing to high protein binding (label); dialysis had no appreciable effect on levels (De Vriese 2015).
